BP CEO thinks the company isn't 'Big Oil' anymore:

"It's prudent for us not to try to label ourselves as a supermajor"

Well, times change: 

2020: "bp’s purpose is to reimagine energy for people and our planet."

2026: "bp is a global oil and gas company."
Oil refining margins fall to 1-month low (arguably, measured by the rather simplistic 3-2-1- WTI crack spread).

CHART OF THE DAY: The cumulative impact of lower Chinese oil imports.

On current trends, by end of August, Beijing would have purchased >450m barrels less than if it had kept its imports at average 2025 levels. The deficit hits ~500m barrels by Nov even with an import recovery. https://t.co/B90tMxAvxh

Qatar Foreign Ministry spokesperson says language for a possible US-Iran interim deal "has been drafted" and "is being circulated between the parties."

The focus is on prevent further escalation, reopen Strait of Hormuz and create conditions to resume Washington-Tehran talks.

BIG OIL 2Q EARNINGS: BP beats estimates, with adj net income of $5.7 billion (and a significant drop in total debt). More important the message from BP new-ish CEO; company needs to do a lot better:

“…Our performance over the past few years has not met our own expectations, let alone those of our shareholders. We have not delivered consistently; we have written off too much value; and our costs and liabilities are not resilient enough in a low price environment…”

She presented 5 priorities ⤵️

Also, BP has put up for sale Archaea Energy, a biogas business that it bought less than four years ago during the green energy bubble for more than $4 billion. Probably another write down in the making.

#Kazakhstan's Tengizchevroil (TCO) plans to export some 100,000 metric tons of oil by rail to Georgia's Black Sea port of Batumi in August, two sources familiar with the company's plans said.

TCO is using alternative, more costly export routes to prevent a further decline in crude output amid unstable exports through the Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC) pipeline, the main export route for Kazakh oil.

As expected, the initial surge of post-MOU inbound ballast (i.e., empty) tankers through Hormuz has entirely faded and the lack of ballast tanker capacity is now again the primary impediment to a recovery in fresh Gulf oil loadings. https://t.co/QTjPWvfEMv

The confirmed volume of oil flowing through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait has fallen by ~40% since the Houthis announced their naval blockade of Saudi shipping

Russian flows holding pretty firm, while Saudi flows are functionally back to prewar (pre-East-West pipeline reroute) levels https://t.co/NprSiLSjx1

Saudi Aramco reported a 44% jump in second-quarter profit to $32.69 billion as higher crude, refined product and chemical prices boosted results amid disruptions from the U.S.-Iran war. CEO Amin Nasser said the company maintained "business continuity" despite "the unprecedented supply disruption through the Strait of Hormuz." - Reuters
Oil price drops amid "renewed peace deal hopes" https://t.co/cbnJEcwicg

Russia has been supplying oil to Syria since the fall of Assad as rent for its continued military presence in Syria; their only such presence along the Med Sea. With Syria now receiving oil by land from Iraq for both domestic consumption and re-exports, Russia finds itself in a bit of a squeeze.

We've tagged a dozen STS transfers of Iraqi crude oil off the east coast of the UAE as well as the coast of Oman since early June 2026 alone. That's around 24 million barrels right there. https://t.co/6C4oFnOCvk
